q: The magnetic field is a region where _____ can be detected.
e: By definition, a magnetic field is the specific region in space where magnetic effects are observable.

q: Distribution of magnetic field can be visualized by the _____.
e: Magnetic lines of force are the conceptual tool used to visualize the distribution and pattern of a magnetic field.

q: The magnetic lines of force leave the _____ pole and enter the south pole.
e: By convention, magnetic lines of force are drawn emerging from the north pole and entering the south pole.

q: To show the pattern of a magnetic field around a bar magnet, we can sprinkle _____ lightly on a paper.
e: Iron filings are used because they are magnetic and will align themselves along the magnetic lines of force.
The Earth itself acts as a giant magnet, possessing its own global magnetic field.

q: We can think of the Earth as having an imaginary bar magnet inside it with magnetic north and _____ poles.
e: The Earth's magnetic field is modeled as an imaginary bar magnet with distinct north and south magnetic poles.

q: The magnetic north lies somewhere in the sea in northern _____ but has been shifting slowly over the years.
e: The Earth's magnetic north pole is geographically located in the sea in northern Canada and shifts over time.

q: A magnetic field has neither a starting point nor an end point because magnets never have a _____.
e: Unlike electric charges, magnetic monopoles do not exist, meaning magnetic field lines always form continuous closed loops.
